subject: Request: Nightly batch headroom amendment for reserved GPUs
messages:
From: Rajesh Menon <rajesh@fastledger.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: FastLedger Platform Ops <platform-ops@fastledger.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Reserved GPU throughput alignment & temporary token-throttle exception

Hi Olga / Redwood team,

Quick context: FastLedger has ramped a nightly batch job that runs inference over long sequences (avg 3K tokens) for our reconciliation pass. Over the last two weekends we’ve hit sustained bursts that exceed our expected concurrency and we’re seeing token-throttle events that pushed tail latency beyond our internal SLOs (and triggered alerts to our on-call).

We have a committed reservation of 4 dedicated GPUs in us-west with a standard queue depth. The throttling behavior looks like the account-level token window + per-tenant queue depth is filling, which causes requests to queue and sometimes retry — that’s what’s spiking our tails.

Ask: Can Redwood provide a short-term carve-out / amendment to increase per-tenant queue depth and enable burst headroom on our reserved pool for 48–72 hours while we run a coordinated mitigation? I’ve attached our demand forecast for the next quarter so you can see the nightly delta. We’re prepared to accept a short-term overage charge but need the throughput guarantee for that window.

Attachments: [Attachment: FastLedger_Demand_Forecast_Q3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 38KB)]

Appreciate an expedited reply — would like to start a pilot this coming Monday (6/21) if possible.

Thanks,
Rajesh Menon
Head of Platform Engineering
FastLedger
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Menon <rajesh@fastledger.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Reserved GPU throughput alignment & temporary token-throttle exception

Rajesh — thanks for the detail and the forecast. We can move quickly here. Short summary of what I’m proposing now so everyone has the same expectations:

- Short-term mitigation (48–72h): enable burst nodes from your dedicated pool (preemptible capacity), increase per-tenant queue depth for your reservation, and relax the account token-throttle window during the window.
- Guardrails: enable canary routing for 10% of traffic and autoscale fallback to a compatible quantized model if headroom is exhausted.
- Commercials: we’ll treat this as a temporary SLA Annex (amendment) that documents the carve-out window and overage billing. Laura — see procurement notes below.

I attached a draft Annex that covers scope, start/stop windows, observability requirements, and rollback criteria. If that looks good, we can run a 30-day pilot and convert to a permanent addendum if metrics are stable.

Attachments: [Attachment: Proposed_SLA_Annex.pdf (document, 22KB)]

Can we schedule a 30-minute call Monday early morning PT to lock start time? Marcus — can you confirm implementation steps and expected risks?

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Customer Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Rajesh Menon <rajesh@fastledger.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Reserved GPU throughput alignment & temporary token-throttle exception

Thanks, Olga. Quick technical note (TL;DR and then specifics): we can do the temporary change but it has trade-offs and we need the forecast to size burst nodes.

TL;DR: Increase per-tenant queue depth from 64 -> 256, allow concurrency-per-tenant up to 8, and provision up to 2 preemptible burst GPUs in the reserved pool for 48h. Monitor tail latency and token-usage. Rollback if median latency degrades >15% or error rate >1%.

Details:
- Why this happens: your nightly batches have long sequences and high per-request token counts; our token-window limit is conservative to protect multi-tenant headroom. When the token-window triggers, requests accumulate in the per-tenant queue, increasing tail latency.
- KV cache helps for prefix-heavy workloads but is not useful for large-batch replays with unique inputs.
- Implementation steps (estimated 2–3 hours):
  1) Apply runtime config: queue_depth=256, max_concurrency=8 for FastLedger tenant ID (non-persistent change).
  2) Provision 2 preemptible GPUs in the dedicated pool and mark as burst-capable for your reservation.
  3) Enable canary routing: 10% traffic on the amended path.
  4) Telemetry: stream token usage, per-tenant queue length, median/tail latency, and error rate to your dashboard.

Risks & notes:
- Cost: burst GPUs are billed as overage; we should capture expected token-surge-to-cost conversion and include in the Annex.
- Contention: if other tenants use burst at the same time, we may hit preemption — we’ll reserve the nodes for the amendment window.
- Fallback: if headroom exhausted, automatic fallback to a compatible 8-bit quantized variant will preserve availability but may slightly change output characteristics.

I’ll prepare a small runbook for operations and a short rollback playbook. If you confirm PO/billing details, we can move to schedule.

—Marcus Lin
Principal Systems Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Menon <rajesh@fastledger.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Reserved GPU throughput alignment & temporary token-throttle exception

Rajesh — procurement/commercial quick steps:

1) Proposed commercial path: 30-day pilot with temporary SLA Annex documenting the 48–72h carve-out windows (can be repeated), overage billing rate, and metrics-based success criteria. If successful, convert to a standing addendum to the Reserved Capacity agreement.
2) We’ll issue a one-time credit equal to 10% of expected overage to offset ramp risk during the pilot.
3) Next items needed from FastLedger: PO number, billing contact, and final signatory for Annex.

Related links: DocuSign envelope prepared: https://app.redwood.com/docusign/FL-2026-08-RSV — please sign after PO is ready. I’ll also attach a short commercial summary to the HubSpot deal.

Action items (for clarity):
- Rajesh: share PO number and billing contact (by Thu 6/17 if you want a Monday 6/21 start).
- Marcus / Olga: confirm SRE runbook & monitoring (ready by end of day Fri).

Thanks — Laura Bennett
Senior Commercial Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Rajesh Menon <rajesh@fastledger.com>

Appreciate the fast turn.

—Rajesh
